article-meta.article-title: Archival Dispatch: 23 Master Broadcasts Dated Across Roy Acuff, Aladdin's Lamp, Benny Goodman, and Let's Pretend
article-meta.kwd-group: Roy Acuff, Grand Ole Opry, Smoky Mountain Boys, Aladdins Lamp, Smilin Ed McConnell, Benny Goodman, Martha Tilton, Peggy Lee, Lets Pretend, Nila Mack, Cream of Wheat, Original Filenames

sec.title: Batch 68 Forensic Discoveries
sec.p: Batch 68 recovers and dates 23 classic radio broadcasts spanning Grand Ole Opry royalty, 1930s singing philosophies, swing era ballroom remotes, and Peabody-winning CBS children's audio dramatizations: 6 high-energy country and western performances from the King of Country Music on ***The Roy Acuff Show*** (1954, sponsored by Royal Crown Cola with the Smoky Mountain Boys), 6 heartwarming acoustic song and story sessions from ***Aladdin's Lamp*** with Smilin' Ed McConnell (1937), 5 classic big band swing recordings from ***Benny Goodman and His Orchestra*** (1937–1941, featuring vocalists Martha Tilton, Helen Forrest, and Peggy Lee), and 6 beloved fairy tale adaptations from Nila Mack's ***Let's Pretend*** (1944–1947, broadcast on CBS for Cream of Wheat).

sec.title: 1. *The Roy Acuff Show* — 1954 Royal Crown Cola Revue
sec.p: Featuring Roy Acuff, Brother Oswald, Jimmy Riddle, and the Smoky Mountain Boys:
sec.table: | Original Circulating Filename | Canonical Title | Verified Airdate | Country & Western Showcase | |---|---|---|---| | `Roy_Acuff_Automobile_Life.mp3` | **"The Roy Acuff Show: 'The Automobile of Life' & Smoky Mountain Boys"** | **1954-04-03** | Classic gospel-bluegrass metaphor song featuring spirited fiddle solos. | | `Roy_Acuff_Profile_Speckled.mp3` | **"The Roy Acuff Show: 'Roy Acuff Profile & Great Speckled Bird'"** | **1954-04-10** | Roy's signature sacred hymn performed for nationwide listeners. | | `Roy_Acuff_Whoa_Mule.mp3` | **"The Roy Acuff Show: 'Whoa Mule Whoa' (RC Cola Revue)"** | **1954-04-17** | Rousing square dance rhythm and comedic banter from the band. | | `Roy_Acuff_Love_Or_Lies.mp3` | **"The Roy Acuff Show: 'Is It Love or Is It Lies'"** | **1954-04-24** | Traditional country ballad harmonized by the Smoky Mountain Boys. | | `Roy_Acuff_Sweet_Love_Die.mp3` | **"The Roy Acuff Show: 'Don't Let Your Sweet Love Die'"** | **1954-05-01** | Driving acoustic guitar and dobro accompaniment on the classic tune. | | `Roy_Acuff_Yall_Come.mp3` | **"The Roy Acuff Show: 'Y'all Come & Grand Ole Opry Fiddle Tune'"** | **1954-05-08** | Welcoming country anthem and fast-paced breakdown fiddling. |
